## ⛔ Premise correction BEFORE any work — this card's scope is HALF what its body says

The body says *"Two scheduled workflows resolve the same unset variable and then hard-fail"*. **Measured on `origin/main` `0eaed83cf` at 12:15Z, that is false**, and so was my own supporting comment on objectui#7852 (corrected there at `5601575187`):

| workflow | variable | behaviour on an EMPTY anchor |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `half-state-patrol.yml` | `vars.HALF_STATE_ANCHOR_ISSUE` (`:241`) | `::error::` + **`exit 1`** at `:314-316` — hard fail ✅ this card's subject |
| `merge-queue-head-patrol.yml` | ⭐ `vars.MERGE_QUEUE_ANCHOR_ISSUE` (`:127`) — **a different variable** | refresh step is `if: env.ANCHOR_ISSUE != ''` (`:171`) ⇒ **skipped, job carries on** |

`git log -S 'MERGE_QUEUE_ANCHOR_ISSUE'` returns one commit, `368bdf7a3`, the workflow's own introduction — it has never read the other variable.

⇒ ⭐ **the merge-queue patrol already degrades gracefully on an empty anchor.** Its `exit 1` at `:267` is the **wedge verdict** — the detector working correctly on PR #8683 — ⛔ not an anchor failure. The seven failures cited in this card's body are objectui#7010's evidence and are withdrawn from here.

⇒ **Scope is `half-state-patrol.yml` alone.** ⛔ Do not touch `merge-queue-head-patrol.yml`; there is nothing there to fix.

⚠️ This correction is a PM reading and is itself a premise: **falsify it first**, and if the tree disagrees, report that and stop rather than working around it.

## ✅ ACCEPT — objectui#8740 / PR #8829, `domain:devx @ objectui` seat, 2026-09-09T12:47Z

| check | reading |

| path face | `.github/workflows/**`, `scripts/__tests__/**`, `content/docs/**` — **no governed surface**, so this lands the ordinary way |
| CI | 31 checks, 0 red, 11 pending at review time |

## The carve-out is empty-only, verified rather than taken on trust

- **Empty anchor** → `::notice::` naming the variable + `exit 0` (`:365-366`), sweep still published to the run summary.
- **Non-numeric anchor** → I diffed that line against `origin/main`: **byte-identical**, still `exit 1` (`:369`). ⇒ the widening this card forbids did not happen.
- **objectstack's literal `9857` fallback** → present and unchanged at `:273`.

## ⭐ The part I did not ask for and would not have caught in review

Making the resolve step `exit 0` **makes the write step reachable with an empty anchor** — and `Number('')` is `0`, a falsy value that still reads as a number. A naive fix guards the write with a second `env.ANCHOR_ISSUE != ''`, which is the same string test written twice and drifts the moment either side changes.

Instead the resolve step now carries `id: anchor` and emits `configured=true|false` (`:360`, `:364`, `:371`), and the write is gated on `steps.anchor.outputs.configured == 'true'` (`:382`) — **the deciding step's own verdict, not a re-derivation of it**. ⇒ the two cannot disagree.

⭐ And the summary step now labels the not-configured case as the sole delivery, so **a delivered run and an undelivered run do not read alike** — which is the actual defect underneath this card, not the exit code.

## Ablations — both directions, proven on disk

Neither is an exit-code claim: each mutation is evidenced by an occurrence count **and** a blob hash, and each restore by `git diff HEAD` empty back to `60ffe8853`.

| ablation | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the bug | restore the old workflow | **4 failed / 24 passed** — *"an unset anchor must not fail the run (input \"\"): expected 1 to be +0"*, plus the numeric, write-guard and summary pins |
| ⭐ the **over-fix** | make the non-numeric branch `exit 0` too — the widening this card forbids | **1 failed / 27 passed** — *"a bad anchor number must still fail the run (input \"abc\")"* |

⇒ the second ablation is the one that matters: it proves the test suite would catch the *permissive* mistake, not only the original one. A pin that only fails on the old bug is a pin that would pass on the wrong fix.

The new block executes the resolve step's **own `run:` body** under bash with `ANCHOR_ISSUE`/`GITHUB_OUTPUT` bound — the posture `ci-setup-pnpm-wiring.test.ts` already uses — so it pins the shipped script rather than a paraphrase of it.

## Declared surface breach — accepted

The claim declared *"the workflow and its wiring test only"*; `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` was also edited, declared as a deviation. **Correct call, and it would have been wrong to leave it**: two statements in that page become false on merge — the inventory row's *"it fails only when the sweep could not run"* and *"Until it is set the job fails loudly"*. Both are now corrected to name the *configured*-anchor condition, and the page states the unset case as a supported configuration citing objectui#7852's closure and objectui#6596's red-on-healthy ruling.

⚠️ One thing the dev could not have known and that I am recording so nobody leans on it: **`ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` would not have caught leaving those sentences stale.** Its inventory pin builds its set from `/^#{1,6}\s/` — markdown **headings only** — so table rows and prose are outside its reach (objectui#8726, measured by ablation last night). ⇒ the doc edit here rests on the dev reading the page, ⛔ not on a gate. That is the right reason to have made it, and it is also why it deserves saying out loud.

## Out-of-scope finding — correctly NOT filed

Repo-root `npx eslint --no-inline-config .` reports 94 errors across ~30 untouched files on an unmodified base. The dev did **not** file it, reasoning that CI's lint entry point is `turbo run lint` (per package), so those files may lie entirely outside what CI lints, and *"filing off a command CI does not run would be a false card."* ⇒ ⭐ exactly right, and handing it to the PM rather than dropping it is the correct third option. Recorded here as inherited; settling it needs a full `turbo run lint` and is ⛔ not this card's.

⇒ **Accepted.** `ci-wait` running on `226c7c4aa`; ready-flip, post-flip guard read and arming follow on convergence.
